# FEATURES  (use these keys in features_enabled / features_disabled):
#   Class: Height
#     Type: Central tendency
#       h_mean               Mean height
#       h_median             Median height
#       h_max                Max height
#       h_p25                Height p25
#       h_p75                Height p75
#       h_p95                Height p95
#     Type: Spread
#       h_var                Height variance
#       h_std                Height std dev
#       h_cv                 Coefficient of variation
#     Type: Shape
#       h_skew               Skewness
#       h_kurtosis           Kurtosis
#     Type: Structure
#       entropy              Vertical entropy
#       sigma_z              Roughness (sigma_z)
#     Type: Density
#       frac_above_mean      Fraction above mean
#       ppr                  Pulse penetration ratio
#   Class: Color
#     Type: Colour
#       R_mean               Mean red
#       G_mean               Mean green
#       B_mean               Mean blue
#   Class: 2D
#     Type: Horizontal (hand-crafted)
#       pca_spread_major     Spread (major axis)
#       pca_spread_minor     Spread (minor axis)
#       pca_anisotropy       Anisotropy
#       asym_major           Asymmetry (major axis)
#       asym_minor           Asymmetry (minor axis)
#       slope_angle_major    Top-bottom angle (major axis)
#       slope_angle_minor    Top-bottom angle (minor axis)
#       rough_major          Directional roughness (major axis)
#       rough_minor          Directional roughness (minor axis)
#
# AUGMENTATION METHODS  (use these keys in augment_selected; ranges as
#   augment_range.<method>.<param> = <min>, <max>):
#   rotation_z     Rotation (vertical axis)  [Geometric]  params: angle_deg
#       range.rotation_z.angle_deg default 0.0 .. 360.0  (Angle (deg))
#   flip_h         Horizontal flip  [Geometric]  params: (no parameters)
#   jitter_xy      x/y jitter  [Noise]  params: sigma_m
#       range.jitter_xy.sigma_m default 0.0 .. 0.02  (Sigma (m))
#   jitter_z       z jitter  [Noise]  params: sigma_m
#       range.jitter_z.sigma_m default 0.0 .. 0.02  (Sigma (m))
#   dropout        Point dropout  [Sampling]  params: fraction
#       range.dropout.fraction default 0.0 .. 0.3  (Drop fraction)
#   bootstrap      Bootstrap resample  [Sampling]  params: n_fraction
#       range.bootstrap.n_fraction default 1.0 .. 1.0  (Size fraction)
# <<< END AUTO-GENERATED REFERENCE <<<

# ====================================================================
# Pipeline configuration — presets of defaults for the first four tabs.
#
# A preset is a NAMED BLOCK:   [name] {  ...settings...  }
# It pre-fills the Setup -> Clipping -> Augmentation -> Feature tabs.
# Pick the active one on the Setup tab (or set `active` below).
#
# Paths are LITERAL: paste a raw Windows path with single backslashes,
# e.g.  cloud_dir = C:\Data\clouds   (no doubling needed).
# Blank value = "use the built-in default". `#` starts a comment line.
# List values are comma-separated; see the reference block above for the
# exact feature keys and augmentation methods/parameters you can use.
# Copy the whole [default] { ... } block to make your own preset.
# ====================================================================

active = SGCBP 2019-10-02

[default] {

    # -- Where each "Browse..." dialog opens -------------------------
    cloud_dir          =
    mask_dir           =
    import_clipped_dir =
    reference_dir      =

    # -- The actual inputs, pre-filled into the Import tab ------------
    # A RELATIVE path is taken from the project root (the folder holding
    # this file), so these keep working on any machine; an absolute path
    # is used as-is. A path that does not exist is simply not filled in.
    # Naming cloud_file/mask_file also selects the "point cloud + masks"
    # route; naming import_folder selects the folder route.
    cloud_file     =
    mask_file      =
    import_folder  =
    reference_file =

    # -- How a plot is IDENTIFIED in external data (imported filenames,
    #    mask attributes, the reference sheet). The app always WRITES
    #    files as plot(N); these only affect what it READS.
    #    The plot number is whatever sits between these two strings:
    label_start = plot(
    label_end   = )
    # Default mask attribute column to read the label from (blank = first):
    label_field =

    # Some datasets identify a plot by its POSITION IN THE FIELD, where
    # neither number is unique on its own (e.g. 12-13-1-b.pcd = row 12,
    # column 13). Turn that on here; label_start/label_end then describe
    # the COLUMN, and these two describe the row.
    use_row         = false
    label_row_start =
    label_row_end   = -

    # -- Importing a folder of per-plot files ------------------------
    # Everything downstream assumes METRES. Must be one of:
    #   Already in metres | Millimetres -> metres |
    #   Centimetres -> metres | Feet -> metres      (blank = metres)
    source_units =
    # Spread plots that all sit on the same origin so they stop
    # overlapping. With use_row on, the real field layout is rebuilt and
    # grid_columns is ignored.
    grid_enabled = false
    grid_columns = 10
    grid_padding = 10.0

    # -- Reference sheet (chosen on the Import tab) ------------------
    # Which column holds the plot number, and (when use_row is on) the
    # row. Blank key column = use the sheet's first column.
    reference_key_column =
    reference_row_column =
    # Keep only the rows where <column> equals <value>. A sheet covering
    # several scan dates lists every plot once per date, which makes the
    # plot number ambiguous — narrow it to one date here.
    reference_filter_column =
    reference_filter_value  =

    # -- Clipping ---------------------------------------------------
    # Text inserted into every clipped file name, right after plot(N):
    universal_string =

    # -- Augmentation -----------------------------------------------
    # Enabled method keys (comma-separated; blank = none pre-selected):
    augment_selected    =
    augment_min_methods = 1
    augment_max_methods = 2
    # Augmented copies per plot (the original is always kept as well):
    augment_copies      = 5
    # Per-method parameter ranges, one line each, e.g.:
    #   augment_range.jitter_z.sigma_m = 0.0, 0.02

    # -- Feature generation -----------------------------------------
    # Point dimension holding height-above-ground. Blank = no forced
    # default: the "Height channel" dropdown pre-selects the first
    # channel detected in the plots. Set e.g. RelativeHeight to
    # pre-select that channel when present.
    height_channel =
    # features_enabled is a whitelist (only these on). When it is blank,
    # features_disabled is a blacklist (all on except these).
    features_enabled  =
    features_disabled =
    # Imported reference columns: same enabled/disabled rule, plus which
    # to one-hot ("split").
    reference_features_enabled  =
    reference_features_disabled =
    reference_features_split    =

    # -- Output file names (no extension; written as .csv) ----------
    feature_table_name      = features
    targets_table_name      = target
    augmentation_table_name = Data augmentation
}


# ====================================================================
# CYENS — one whole-field cloud per date, cut with a GeoPackage of plot
# masks. Plots carry a single real id (the gpkg's `plot` column, 429...),
# and the workbook is keyed on the same number, so no row/column pair and
# no unit conversion are needed.
# ====================================================================
[CYENS] {

    cloud_dir          = Data/CYENS
    mask_dir           = Data/CYENS
    import_clipped_dir =
    reference_dir      = Data/CYENS

    cloud_file     = Data/CYENS/03_04_2025/03-04-2025_pre_processed.las
    mask_file      = Data/CYENS/final mask remapped.gpkg
    import_folder  =
    reference_file = Data/CYENS/Cyens data Sept2025.xlsx

    # The gpkg stores a bare integer, so no surrounding text to strip.
    label_start =
    label_end   =
    label_field = plot
    use_row     = false

    # Blank = detect. The .las declares UTM zone 36N, whose axis unit is the
    # metre, so detection reads it straight off the file's own CRS. The clip
    # route keeps real coordinates, so there is nothing to lay out either.
    source_units =
    grid_enabled = false

    # Cyens data Sept2025.xlsx is keyed on F.PLT and covers one date, so
    # no row column and no row filter.
    reference_key_column    = F.PLT
    reference_row_column    =
    reference_filter_column =
    reference_filter_value  =

    universal_string =

    augment_selected    =
    augment_min_methods = 1
    augment_max_methods = 2
    augment_copies      = 5

    height_channel =
    # Every feature on: this cloud carries RGB, so the colour features are
    # real measurements here (both lists blank = the whole set enabled).
    features_enabled  =
    features_disabled =
    reference_features_enabled  =
    reference_features_disabled =
    reference_features_split    =
    target_column = Fresh weight (kg per hectare)
    outer_split_mode = random_systematic
    inner_split_mode = random_systematic

    feature_table_name      = features
    targets_table_name      = target
    augmentation_table_name = Data augmentation
}


# ====================================================================
# SGCBP (Yanco 2019) — early scan, 2019-08-28 (stage Z31).
#
# Per-plot .pcd files, one folder per driving run. A plot is identified by
# its grid position: 12-13-1-b.pcd is run 12, range 13. The range alone
# repeats across every run (18 ranges, ~230 plots), so BOTH numbers are
# needed — for uniqueness, to key the ground truth, and to rebuild the
# field layout.
#
# The two scan dates share one ground-truth file and one set of
# (runNo, rangeNo) keys, so each date has its own preset here: the only
# differences are the folder and the stage filter. Mixing them would make
# every plot number ambiguous.
# ====================================================================
[SGCBP 2019-08-28] {

    cloud_dir          =
    mask_dir           =
    import_clipped_dir = Data/SGCBP/original/Yanco_TC_2019_HI-pcd
    reference_dir      = Data/SGCBP/original

    cloud_file     =
    mask_file      =
    import_folder  = Data/SGCBP/original/Yanco_TC_2019_HI-pcd/20190828
    reference_file = Data/SGCBP/original/Ground_truth_data_final.csv

    # 12-13-1-b.pcd -> row 12, column 13.
    use_row         = true
    label_row_start =
    label_row_end   = -
    label_start     = -
    label_end       = -1-b
    label_field     =

    # Stated, not detected: .pcd files declare no coordinate system, and
    # these coordinates are millimetres while the feature stack assumes
    # metres. Every plot is stored re-centred on its own origin, so the
    # layout is rebuilt from the run/range numbers.
    source_units = Millimetres -> metres
    grid_enabled = true
    grid_columns = 18
    grid_padding = 10.0

    # Ground_truth_data_final.csv is keyed on (runNo, rangeNo) and holds
    # both dates — every pair appears twice, so this filter is what keeps
    # the join unambiguous.
    reference_key_column    = rangeNo
    reference_row_column    = runNo
    reference_filter_column = stage
    reference_filter_value  = Z31

    universal_string =

    augment_selected    =
    augment_min_methods = 1
    augment_max_methods = 2
    augment_copies      = 5

    # The .pcd files carry no height-above-ground channel, so the plain Z
    # is the height. Stated explicitly: left blank, the dropdown falls back
    # to the file's first dimension, which is X.
    height_channel = Z
    # The .pcd files carry x/y/z + intensity only, so the three colour
    # features are switched off — left on they would be all-NaN columns.
    features_enabled  =
    features_disabled = R_mean, G_mean, B_mean
    # Nothing from the reference sheet is pre-ticked: which of its columns
    # become features is the user's call, made on the Feature tab. Ticking
    # any of them here would silently put sheet columns into X - and for
    # biomass_g_mSq, the target itself, that is straight label leakage.
    # (If you do tick trt, a categorical treatment code, also tick "split"
    # so it is one-hot encoded rather than read as a number.)
    reference_features_enabled  =
    reference_features_disabled =
    reference_features_split    =
    target_column = biomass_g_mSq
    outer_split_mode = random_systematic
    inner_split_mode = random_systematic

    feature_table_name      = features
    targets_table_name      = target
    augmentation_table_name = Data augmentation
}
